heading: Street corners and conference stages.
sub: He speaks the same way on both.
paragraphs: Most speakers on youth, leadership or resilience have either lived it or studied it. Nahim has done both, and he’s still doing the work on a Tuesday night in Poplar.
That’s what changes a room. There’s no gap between the story and the storyteller. Young people spot that instantly. So do senior leaders, once they’ve stopped expecting a motivational speech.
He’s spoken alongside the Mayor of London, in lecture theatres, at national youth-sector events and in school halls. He adapts to the room, but he doesn’t change the message.

topics.title: Youth work
topics.blurb: What it actually is, why it’s the most undervalued profession in the country, and what the rest of the world could learn from it.

topics.title: Young people
topics.blurb: Why “hard to reach” is usually a description of the institution, not the young person. And what reaching them really takes.

topics.title: Leadership
topics.blurb: Leadership isn’t a title. It’s how you show up when nobody’s watching, and whether you reach back once you’ve made it forward.

topics.title: Resilience and wellbeing
topics.blurb: For the people who pour everything into others. How to keep going in high-pressure work without burning out, from someone who nearly did.

topics.title: Purpose
topics.blurb: Nahim has seen what happens to people who live without it. This is about finding yours, and helping others find theirs.

topics.title: Community and social change
topics.blurb: Building the village. What sustainable change looks like in places affected by poverty, violence and deprivation, from someone who grew up in one.

topics.title: Opportunity and inclusion
topics.blurb: Who gets opportunities and who doesn’t. What it took to get from no GCSEs to four universities, and why it shouldn’t have been that hard.
